To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cytocompatibility characteristics of polyurethane membrane biosensors can be significantly influenced by antimicrobial treatments, such as UV or gamma irradiation or treatment with hydrogen peroxid-containing solutions.
the antimicrobial treatments of polyurethane glucose biosensor membranes have a significant influence on their cytocompatibility characteristics.
the cytocompatibility in vivo is influenced not only by the biomaterial itself but also by the antimicrobial treatments applied to the biomaterial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of biosensor membranes which are biocompatible and which can be sterilized by gamma irradiation.
the cytocompatibility and biocompatibility of polymeric materials for biomedical applications.
the development of a novel glucose biosensor for the continuous monitoring of blood glucose in diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytocompatibility characteristics of a biomaterial should be evaluated in a well-defined manner and that the results should be compared to a reference biomaterial.
cytocompatibility is influenced by the type and extent of treatment.

all of the antimicrobial methods investigated are suitable for the preparation of polyurethane membrane-based glucose sensors, but that the method of choice should be determined according to the application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytocompatibility characteristics of the membrane materials were not influenced by irradiation, while cytotoxicity of membrane extracts was not observed.
the antimicrobial treatment of polyurethane biomaterials should be performed with care and the cytocompatibility characteristics should be tested for the specific treatment applied.
the antimicrobial treatment of biosensor membranes should not only be effective against the target bacteria but also cytocompatible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antimicrobial treatment of biosensor membranes should not be performed without taking into account its cytocompatibility.
cytocompatibility of a biomaterial is not only dependent on the material but also upon the antimicrobial treatments which may influence the bioperformance characteristics of the biomaterial.
cytocompatibility is not a material property but a function of the material, its processing and its environment.
